comment: Checkovich's class is an easy B but a hard A. He assigns interesting yet long readings but he's a great lecturer and if you pay attention you'll be fine. He assigns 3 papers that emphasize critical thinking and the learning curve is steep with these papers, so figure them out fast. Participating in class and going to office hours goes a long way.

Readings were super interesting, but instead of talking about the mind boggling or progressive topics, discussions were centered around questions like "what is the historian trying to communicate?" While the essays were not required to be too long in length, I found the prompts difficult to understand.

Checkovich is an amazing professor. He is funny, smart, and extremely helpful. Most of your grade depends on three essays throughout the year and they are not too hard to write. Participation is also important to just say one or two things every class in order to get a good grade in participation. Be prepared for a crap ton of reading.

Dr. Checkovich is absolutely amazing. He is just trying to get you to think critically. This class challenged my cognitive boundaries, and pushed me to explore new ways of thinking. Lots of reading, but you can get by with skimming. Class discussion everyday which he makes very interesting. Go see him for essays, he is very helpful.

Dr. Checkovich is a really nice guy, but I did not enjoy his style of teaching. I took the Health in American History class. The topic was fairly interesting, but class consisted of the same people making comments all of the time about the readings. Feedback on papers was not the most helpful. Also, he is very big on interaction during class.

I took his Nature in American History class for my gen ed requirement and I would do it again. No tests; just 3 papers. Lots of reading and participation is important. I tried to speak once a class/week and that seemed to be ok. Really funny guy. Thick material but not too difficult and he makes it much more interesting. Good class and cool teacher

Prof. Checkovich's Hist 199 class was one of the most intriguing I have ever taken. He really makes you think about how and why the world works. I have gained a whole new perspective and tool set on how to evaluate things that transcends all subjects. I think it is a class every student should take, regardless of their field of study.

The course consists of three papers, it is difficult to get an A in the course. It was hard to find what he was looking for. I did not find the readings to be too interesting and Class Participation consisted of the same few people making comments.

Awesome teacher and extremely interestingriveting course. Fantastic at swaying conversation towards his main objective while still allowing students to display their opinion. Participate and listen to his points carefully and you can definitely get A's . I definitely recommend taking his course

Health in American History- His teaching style, and class are a breath of fresh air. The more readings you do, the better understanding of the topic and what he expects. You will get an A in participation by reading a few articles per class, just speak and get points for your opinion. All he wants from his students is for us to THINK, and QUESTION.

Readings and three papers that go up in length with each assignment. Poses a question and lets class direct from there, only intruding to steer discussion when it begins to go off course. Barely read anything. He has a very odd and dark sense of humor that he tries to hide under his professionalism but he hilariously slips occasionally.

Grade was 3 short essays and class participation, no tests. Easy B on essays but almost impossible to get an A. Class participation is graded daily and makes attendance important, but you can get by without doing all of the nightly reading.

Checkovich is really laid back and allows the class to run the discussion.  Even if you have trouble communicating a thought he helps reword your ideas so you don't look like a crazy person.  You have a couple of  papers that are fairly easy to write and as for homework it is only reading but nothing you have to turn in.

20th cent amer fic: i LOVED discussions, worked my butt of reading closely to be major particpant in class. his essays are obnoxious. 3 short papers, but he expected answers like "the question you're asking cant be asnwered", if u wrote solid essay w LOTS of proof, stamp grade: B w/ comment "i know this". managed B+ b/c of partic; put in work of A+

Make sure you talk in class...participation is huge. Mostly reading and discussion with a few short papers. Checkovich can be hard to read at sometimes, like you can't always tell what he wants. Not an easy A, but without a lot of work could definitly pull off a B.

If you don't like to participate-don't take this class. The topic sounds interesting but the whole class consists of a roundtable discussion, where the teacher makes you feel guilty for not saying something. Also, each session requires a ton of reading.

LOVE HIM. Had him for technology in American history and grew to love the class. Great lecturer, great at facilitating conversation. Be prepared to read about 40 pages prior to each class. However, reading is not vital as I got by without doing a lot and pulled an A.
